headline: 10-Year U.S. Treasury Bond Yield Surpasses Five Percent
summary: The 10-year US Treasury yield has risen above 5%, a level not seen since before the 2007 financial crisis. Rising oil prices and inflation are cited as drivers, affecting borrowing costs and forecasts.
why: The 10-year Treasury yield is the benchmark for US long-term borrowing costs and is widely used to price mortgages, corporate debt and equity valuations.
why_moved: The article attributes the rise in yields to higher oil prices and inflation, which raise expectations for borrowing costs and bond investors' required returns.
